issues.title: Six OpenClaw Vulnerabilities (Endor Labs Research)
issues.notes: Endor Labs disclosed six vulnerabilities on Feb 18, 2026: CVE-2026-26322 (SSRF in Gateway tool, CVSS 7.6), CVE-2026-26319 (missing Telnyx webhook auth, CVSS 7.5), CVE-2026-26329 (path traversal in browser upload, HIGH), GHSA-56f2-hvwg-5743 (SSRF in image tool, CVSS 7.6), GHSA-pg2v-8xwh-qhcc (SSRF in Urbit auth, CVSS 6.5), GHSA-c37p-4qqg-3p76 (Twilio webhook auth bypass, CVSS 6.5). Patched in 2026.2.17 per CybersecurityNews report. We run 2026.2.19-2 (newer). Our exposure: Gateway/image/browser tools potentially in use; we do NOT use Telnyx, Urbit, or Twilio. Key lesson: Validation must occur at every layer; LLM outputs and tool parameters are attack surfaces.

issues.title: Vidar Infostealer Stealing OpenClaw Config Files (First In-the-Wild)
issues.notes: First confirmed in-the-wild Vidar infostealer variant stealing OpenClaw config files (incident: Feb 13, 2026; reported: Feb 16-17 by BleepingComputer, THN, CybersecurityNews). NOT a targeted OpenClaw attack — broad file-grabbing routine scanning for 'token'/'private key' keywords and '.openclaw' directory. Stolen: openclaw.json (gateway tokens), device.json (private keys), soul.md, memory files. Our risk: server-side Linux deployment — primary infection vector is workstation malware. We have no interactive user sessions on the server. Still: if server were compromised, all these files would be at risk. Recommend: verify file permissions on /root/clawd, review any token rotation schedule.
reportAgainIf: Our tokens appear in any breach database
Broad file-grab campaign specifically targeting servers (not workstations)
OpenClaw releases mitigation (e.g., encrypted config, token rotation)

issues.title: Node.js qs Library Comma Parsing DoS
issues.notes: Logic flaw in Node.js 'qs' library (query string parser). When comma parsing is enabled, crafted requests with thousands of commas force massive array allocations, causing DoS/crash. Published Feb 12 2026. We run Node.js v22.22.0. Our exposure is low: we don't run a user-facing HTTP server with qs query string processing. If openclaw or any dependency uses qs with comma parsing enabled, we could be affected. No patch confirmed yet.
reportAgainIf: We confirm we use qs with comma parsing enabled

issues.title: OpenClaw Remote Code Execution
issues.notes: Token exfiltration via malicious links. We are patched.

issues.title: OpenClaw Docker Sandbox Escape
issues.notes: Docker sandbox escape via PATH manipulation. PATCH CONFIRMED in 2026.1.29 (announced 2026-02-09 by SecurityScorecard/The Register). We run 2026.2.15, fully patched. Public PoC remains available on GitHub.

issues.title: OpenClaw SSH Command Injection (macOS)
issues.notes: SSH command injection in macOS app. We run Linux only, not affected.

issues.title: Mass OpenClaw Internet Exposure
issues.notes: Exposure count grew from 40.2K (Feb 12) to 135,000+ as of Feb 9 (SecurityScorecard / The Register). ~15K vulnerable to RCE. We are localhost-only, not exposed. APT correlation still present (Kimsuky, APT28). OpenAI acquisition of OpenClaw (Feb 15) may affect future security posture.
reportAgainIf: Our instance appears in exposure scans
New attack vectors targeting localhost deployments

issues.title: ClawHub Malicious Skills Campaign
issues.notes: Second wave confirmed Feb 2-13 2026: 341 new malicious skills (The Hacker News), additional hundreds tracked by VirusTotal and Bitdefender. Automated upload scripts still active as of early Feb (Bitdefender). Targeting macOS/Windows. Our installed skills (youtube-extraction, ai-creator-scan) verified legitimate. Conscia report (Feb 18, 2026) now confirms 824+ malicious skills across an expanded registry of 10,700+ (~20% of registry). Still install vetted skills only.
reportAgainIf: One of our installed skills flagged

issues.title: Node.js January 2026 Security Release (Multiple High CVEs)
issues.notes: Jan 13 2026 release patched 3 High + 4 Medium CVEs: CVE-2025-55131 (buffer uninitialized memory), CVE-2025-55130 (fs permission bypass via symlinks), CVE-2025-59465 (HTTP/2 DoS crash), CVE-2026-21636 (UDS permission bypass). We run v22.22.0 which IS the security patch release.

issues.title: OpenAI Acquires OpenClaw / Peter Steinberger Joins OpenAI
issues.notes: Sam Altman announced Feb 15/16 2026: Peter Steinberger (OpenClaw creator) joining OpenAI. OpenClaw to transition to open-source foundation with OpenAI support. Security implications: update cadence, governance, and code ownership may change. Monitor for changes to update/release policy.

issues.title: AI Recommendation Poisoning via Hidden Prompt Injection in Web Content
issues.notes: Microsoft Security Blog (Feb 10, 2026): 31 companies discovered embedding hidden instructions in 'Summarize with AI' buttons. When clicked, these inject persistence commands into AI assistant memory via URL prompt parameters (MITRE ATLAS AML.T0080, AML.T0051). Goal: bias AI recommendations toward their products. Directly relevant to OpenClaw deployments with memory tools and web browsing. Our setup: Hugo has web browsing capability, memory system (MEMORY.md, daily notes). Risk: malicious page visited during web research could inject into memory. Mitigations: we don't have persistent cross-session 'AI memory' in the cloud-sync sense; memory is file-based and reviewed by Thomas. Still: be cautious when browsing unknown pages with explicit instructions to 'remember' things.
reportAgainIf: Specific OpenClaw memory poisoning PoC published
Exploitation confirmed against local AI agents
ATLAS updates guidance for this vector

issues.title: Promptware Kill Chain Framework — Indirect Prompt Injection as Multi-Stage Attack
issues.notes: Lawfare/Schneier (Feb 13-14, 2026), arxiv paper: Researchers formalize a 7-step kill chain for 'promptware' attacks on LLM-based systems. Key insight: indirect prompt injection (via web pages, emails, documents, images) is more dangerous than direct injection, allowing C2-style persistent control of AI agents. Multimodal inputs (images, audio) expand the attack surface. Directly relevant to autonomous AI agents like OpenClaw. No new CVE; this is academic framing. Our mitigations: external content is wrapped with UNTRUSTED warnings in our config, system prompts enforce safety rules. Thomas reviews memory files.
reportAgainIf: OpenClaw-specific kill chain PoC or active exploit published
Specific mitigation or patch released for this class of attack
